scoring_justification: Agent outputs only predicted G_IRs; no raw intermediate artifacts available for recompute. Compare predicted values to hidden experimental gold (Table 5) with tolerance-based reward for Kevlar (threshold_or_better), directional check for carbon, and monotonic trend verification.

hidden_assets.purpose: Experimental steady-state G_IRs from paper Table 5 used as hidden gold for scoring the agent's predicted values
hidden_assets.generation_method: Copied directly from paper Table 5 values (mean values), rounded to two decimals as reported.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the actual published experimental measurements the paper claims the model should reproduce. They provide the authentic gold standard.

outputs.description: Predicted steady-state mode I delamination toughness values for stitched laminate configurations listed in the paper's Table 6. The values are compared to experimental measurements (hidden) with a tolerance on relative error for Kevlar threads, and a directional check for carbon threads. Monotonic trends with stitch density and thread diameter are also verified.

steps.description: File exists with required columns and exactly 8 rows
Score Kevlar configurations by relative error against experimental gold; full credit if relative error <= 20%, linear decay to 0 at 100% error
For carbon threads, predicted G_IRs must be lower than experimental (underprediction)
Check monotonic trends: within each thread family, higher stitch density gives higher G_IRs; at fixed density 4 st/cm², larger thread diameter gives higher G_IRs
